questions.article: Technological advances have prompted companies to increasingly rely on automation to streamline production. questions.article:
Text 1
To many artists in the mid-nineteenth-century United States, the American wilderness symbolized innocence and untouched beauty. So George Inness's decision to foreground a railroad in his 1855 painting The Lackawanna Valley is notable, since images of railroads often alluded to the destruction of wilderness in the name of progress. In fact, art historian Nicolai Cikovsky Jr. argues that Inness glorifies the subject of the railroad by painting a scene that suggests hopefulness rather than devastation.

Text 2
It is impossible to deduce anything about George Inness's personal views from The Lackawanna Valley because the painting was a commissioned work for the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad, intended to promote the company's expansion. As a result, the painting's content likely reflects commercial demands rather than the artist's own artistic intentions.
questions.question: Which choice best describes a difference in how the author of Text 1 and the author of Text 2 view the painting The Lackawanna Valley?

options.name: A
options.content: The author of Text 1 implies that the styles and themes of the painting are atypical of Inness's body of work, whereas the author of Text 2 claims that the painting is representative of Inness as a painter.

options.name: B
options.content: The author of Text 1 suggests that the painting can reveal information about lnness's opinions, whereas the author of Text 2 believes that the circumstances of the painting's production prohibit such an interpretation.

options.name: C
options.content: The author of Text 1 claims that the painting is an accurate representation of a physical place, whereas the author of Text 2 identifies several embellishments that Inness made to alter the scene.

options.name: D
options.content: The author of Text 1 focuses on the painting's symbolic representation of technological progress, whereas the author of Text 2 emphasizes its realistic portrayal of industrial development.

questions.correct: The author of Text 1 suggests that the painting can reveal information about lnness's opinions, whereas the author of Text 2 believes that the circumstances of the painting's production prohibit such an interpretation.

questions.article: The prints in Images of Autonomous Matter, part of a traveling exhibition of innovative Japanese art from the 1960s and 1970s, exemplify the interest in creating minimalist images of stark materials, such as steel, that first emerged among Japanese printmakers in the mid-to-late twentieth century. Mitsuo Kano's close-up of a serrated metal fragment, Soldered Blue, and Tatsuo Kawaguchi's image of a single corroded staple, which belongs to his Relation-Quality series, are two such works in the exhibit. In their emphasis on the innate qualities of manufactured materials, both prints push traditional boundaries for figurative art.
questions.question: Which statement about the prints by Kano and Kawaguchi in Images of Autonomous Matter is best supported by the text?

options.name: A
options.content: The portrayal of imperfection in the prints illustrates that the artists' goal was to disrupt the carefully curated nature of most art exhibitions.

options.name: B
options.content: The objects depicted and the manner of depiction render the prints distinct from more conventional works of art.

options.name: C
options.content: The prints showcase how different methods for printing images can offer unique perspectives on stark materials.

options.name: D
options.content: The prints emulate the style of an earlier artistic movement that used simplistic compositions and featured industrial objects.

questions.correct: The objects depicted and the manner of depiction render the prints distinct from more conventional works of art.

questions.article: Arturo Casadevall et al. have confirmed that twenty mushroom species (including Marasmius capillaris and species from the genus Russula) maintain subambient temperatures in both their fruited bodies and their mycelium (the root-like hyphae from which the fruited bodies grow), though the benefits of this hypothermic behavior are unclear. Noting that relative coldness was more pronounced in fruiting than in nonfruiting sites of the myceliumâa difference that persisted even after fruited bodies were detachedâthe researchers speculate that thermoregulation in the mycelium may influence reproductive success.
questions.question: Which statement about the mycelium of the twenty mushroom species is best supported by the text?

options.name: A
options.content: The mycelium generally maintains temperatures lower than those of the fruited bodies even when considering temperature variations between fruiting and nonfruiting sites.

options.name: B
options.content: The correlation between higher mycelium temperature and greater fruit productivity indicates that successful reproduction may be dependent on thermoregulation in the mycelium.

options.name: C
options.content: Variation in thermoregulation across the mycelium may occur independent of the presence or absence of fruited bodies.

options.name: D
options.content: Temperatures in the fruiting areas of one mycelium are lower than in the nonfruiting areas due to differences in the depth and spread of the mycelium within soil or other organic matter.

questions.correct: Variation in thermoregulation across the mycelium may occur independent of the presence or absence of fruited bodies.

questions.article:
The following text is from William Carlos Williams's 1925 creative nonfiction book In the American Grain. Williams is discussing how works by nineteenth-century US poet and fiction writer Edgar Allan Poe were received by American readers.

Poe must suffer by his originality. Invent that which is new, even if it be made of pine from your own yard, and there's none to know what you have done. It is because there's no name. This is the cause of Poe's lack of recognition. He was American. He was the astounding, inconceivable growth of his locality. Gape at him they did, and he at them in amazement. Afterward with mutual hatred; he in disgust, they in mistrust. It is only that which is under your nose that seems most difficult to see.
questions.question: What does the text most strongly suggest about Poe's work and American readers?

options.name: A
options.content: Poe's work was so innovative that there was not even terminology to describe it, which led American readers to regard both the work and Poe himself as strange but quintessentially American.

options.name: B
options.content: Poe's work had few fans among American readers because it tended to present a negative image of American life and institutions.

options.name: C
options.content: American readers largely ignored Poe's work because its tone and subject matter were out of keeping with mainstream literature.

options.name: D
options.content: American readers failed to appreciate Poe's work because of its novelty and the fact that it reflected aspects of the American character too ingrained in those readers for them to comprehend.

questions.correct: American readers failed to appreciate Poe's work because of its novelty and the fact that it reflected aspects of the American character too ingrained in those readers for them to comprehend.

questions.article: The percent of cities and towns in a given period that persist from a prior period (backward continuity) and the percent that persist into a later period (forward continuity) are known to correlate positively with economic and political stability in a region. Researchers studying demographic trends in the Indigenous societies of ancient Mexico determined both continuity measures for the Yautepec Valley, which lay within the macroregional hegemony of the city-state of Teotihuacan from roughly 100 BCE until roughly 450 CE, after which point Teotihuacan declined. options.name: B

options.name: C
options.content: Teotihuacan's hegemony imposed stability on the Yautepec Valley mitigating the decrease in the compound average annual growth rate of the valley's population as well as the decrease in the number of cities and towns there in the Early Classic and Middle Classic.

options.name: D
options.content: although the forward continuity data suggest that the decline of Teotihuacan occasioned economic and political instability in the Yautepec Valley, these developments were nonetheless associated with a net increase in the valley's population.

questions.correct: although the forward continuity data suggest that the decline of Teotihuacan occasioned economic and political instability in the Yautepec Valley, these developments were nonetheless associated with a net increase in the valley's population.

questions.article: In an analysis of medieval urbanization in Pisa, Greifswald, and other European settlements, researchers drew on modern urban scaling theory, which posits that population density in core urban areas increases as a city grows larger. Hypothesizing that this typical relationship would have differed in medieval settlements because of the constraining influence of strong hierarchical social structures (which are much less pronounced in modern cities) on social networking and economic integrationâdrivers of urban agglomerationâthe team created a model that accounted for the presence of restrictive institutions. They found that the typically expected density-size relationship held for each of the 173 medieval settlements whose growth they analyzed, suggesting that ______
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.name: A
options.content: the social and economic dynamics that affect urban agglomeration were likely much different in medieval settlements than in modern cities, despite the similarity across time in population density patterns.

options.name: B
options.content: although there tends to be a positive relationship between population size and development of core urban areas for both medieval settlements and modern cities, social institutions likely limited the rate at which population density increased in medieval settlements.

options.name: C
options.content: despite a change in the role of social structures over time, there is likely a notable consistency between medieval settlements and modern cities in underlying elements of the social and economic interactions among individuals that shape the development of core urban areas.

options.name: D
options.content: the constraining influence of hierarchical medieval institutions likely had a significant effect on individuals in some social groupings but little to no effect on members of other social groupings.

questions.correct: despite a change in the role of social structures over time, there is likely a notable consistency between medieval settlements and modern cities in underlying elements of the social and economic interactions among individuals that shape the development of core urban areas.

questions.article:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Birthday Party is a 1957 black-and-white linocut print by Black American artist Margaret Burroughs.
  • It depicts a tranquil, everyday scene (a group of children celebrating).
  • Amanzi Amthatha (âThe cold water takes himâ) is a 2001 black-and-white linocut print by South African artist Nomathemba Tana.
  • It features a scene with an explicitly political point of view (a Xhosa warrior fighting British colonial rule).
  • Relief printing is a technique in which an image is carved onto a printing block, covered in ink or paint, and stamped.
questions.question: The student wants to contrast the subject matter of the two prints. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.name: A
options.content: The print by Tana is a black-and-white linocut; by contrast, Burroughs's is a relief print.

options.name: B
options.content: Burroughs made Birthday Party in 1957, while Tana made Amanzi Amthatha (âThe cold water takes himâ) later, in 2001.

options.name: C
options.content: Tana's print expresses an explicitly political point of view, while Burroughs's depicts a tranquil, everyday scene.

options.name: D
options.content: The scenes depicted in both works were first carved onto a printing block, then stamped onto paper; however, one work is a linocut, while the other is a relief print.

questions.correct: Tana's print expresses an explicitly political point of view, while Burroughs's depicts a tranquil, everyday scene.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Researchers Gwangsu Kim et al. sought to explore the relationship between the brain's ability to process natural sounds and its ability to process music.
  • They used an artificial deep neural network (DNN) that models how the brain processes auditory information.
  • The DNN had been trained to detect natural sounds (excluding music).
  • Finding: The DNN spontaneously developed neurons that responded to music but not to other auditory stimuli.
  • Conclusion: The brain's ability to process music may arise as a by-product of natural sound processing.
questions.question: The student wants to present the aim of the study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.name: A
options.content: Using an artificial deep neural network, the researchers sought to explore the relationship between the brain's ability to process natural sounds and its ability to process music.

options.name: B
options.content: The researchers used an artificial deep neural network, which spontaneously developed neurons that respond to music but not to other auditory stimuli.

options.name: C
options.content: By training an artificial deep neural network, the researchers aimed to establish that the brain's ability to process natural sounds arises as a by-product of processing music.

options.name: D
options.content: The researchers used an artificial deep neural network to demonstrate that neurons responding to music are also sensitive to a wide range of other auditory stimuli.

questions.correct: Using an artificial deep neural network, the researchers sought to explore the relationship between the brain's ability to process natural sounds and its ability to process music.
